vulnerabilities.description: Plain-text storage of sensitive data. Memory data including user calculations and context is stored in JSON files without encryption at .claude-flow/data/memory.json
vulnerabilities.impact: Sensitive user data could be exposed if file permissions are incorrect or system is compromised

vulnerabilities.description: Session files stored with default file permissions in .claude-flow/sessions/. No encryption of session context data
vulnerabilities.impact: Session data including user context could be readable by other system users on shared systems

vulnerabilities.description: No input size validation on memory values. Unlimited data can be stored without checks
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential DoS through unbounded memory storage

vulnerabilities.description: Temporary files created in system tmpdir without explicit permission restrictions. On multi-user systems, TOCTOU race condition possible
vulnerabilities.impact: Another process on the system could theoretically read the temporary file before deletion (low probability)

vulnerabilities.description: Session files stored in project directory (.claude-flow/sessions/). Could be accidentally committed to version control
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential exposure of session context data through git history

recommendations: Encrypt sensitive data stored in .claude/helpers/memory.js using a standard encryption library (e.g., crypto module)
Implement file permission restrictions on session/memory files: chmod 600 or equivalent to restrict to owner only
Add input validation and size limits to memory.js set() function to prevent unbounded storage
Add .claude-flow/ directory to .gitignore to prevent accidental commits of session/memory files containing sensitive data
Consider using temporary file libraries (e.g., tmp package) that handle secure temp file creation with proper permissions
Add encryption for temporary files created in github-safe.js before writing sensitive body content
Implement secure file cleanup with multiple retry attempts in finally block to ensure tmpfiles are removed
Add security headers for any API endpoints (though this appears to be a static site, verify if API routes exist)
Audit git history for any committed secrets: git log --all -p | grep -i 'password\|secret\|key\|token'
Add pre-commit hooks to prevent secrets from being committed

secretsAndCredentials.details: No hardcoded API keys, passwords, or credentials found in source code

xssVulnerabilities.details: No direct XSS vulnerabilities. React/Next.js properly escapes content by default

commandInjection.details: github-safe.js properly uses spawnSync() instead of shell execution, preventing shell injection

authentication.details: No authentication mechanisms present. Static site - not applicable

dataProtection.details: Sensitive data stored in plain text without encryption in memory.js and session.js

filePermissions.details: Session and memory files may be readable by other system users due to default umask

implemented: Input validation on keys in memory.js and session.js
Safe command execution using spawnSync instead of shell
No eval() or dangerous dynamic code execution
missing: Encryption for sensitive data at rest
File permission restrictions on sensitive files
